content.text: Black Mariah is an umbrella name for several Seven Card Stud poker variants that all revolve around the Queen of Spades or spades in general. In the most distinctive version, a player must hold BOTH the best poker hand AND the highest spade at showdown to win the pot. If those two conditions are met by different players, or if no one holds spades, nobody wins and the pot carries over â€” making it a potentially monster pot that grows across multiple deals.

Black Mariah emerged from American home poker games as one of several Seven Card Stud variants using the Queen of Spades (Qâ™ ) or spades generally as a special mechanic. The name 'Black Mariah' (or 'Maria') is also used in Hearts to refer to the Qâ™ . The poker variant shares this dramatic association.

Two to eight players. This version of Black Mariah is a seven card stud variant; as in standard stud, the usual number is two to eight so that each player receives seven cards from a single 52-card deck. Only players who were in the showdown participate in the next deal when the pot has carried over.
Standard Seven Card Stud deal: 2 cards face-down, 4 face-up, 1 face-down. Betting rounds after each up-card.

items.text: The Bitch (Alternative Black Mariah): Black Mariah is sometimes used as an alternative name for The Bitch, where Qâ™  face-up kills the deal.
Follow the Queen + Kill (Alternative): Some play Black Mariah as Follow the Queen but with the Qâ™  kill mechanic from The Bitch.
High Chicago (Alternative Name): Sometimes Black Mariah is used as an alternative name for High Chicago (highest spade in the hole splits pot).
